packet: TS Water Harvesting L3 body candidate
sourceBody: Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.
Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.
Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.
Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.
The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.
Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.
List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
currentDraftBody: Lwangu ra wena ri nga hlengeleta mati ya mpfula. Ntsengo wu titshege hi vukulu bya lwangu, mpfula na ku lahleka ka mati.
Kamba loko switirhisiwa swa lwangu swi faneleka ku hlengeleta mati ya mpfula u nga si hlanganisa thanki.

Tirhisa vukulu bya lwangu loko ri langutiwa hi le henhla na tirhekhodo ta mpfula ya le kusuhi. Kutani u tekela enhlokweni mati lama hundzaka gatara, lama hambukisiwaka kumbe lama halakaka loko thanki yi tele.
Ntsengo wa lembe hinkwaro a wu ku byeli leswaku ku ta va na mati yo tanihi kwihi hi nkarhi wa dyandza. Pimanisa mati lama nga kona na mitirho leyi u yi kunguhataka.
Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.
The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.
Sayizi ya thanki yi titshege hi xilaveko xa mati, mpfula, vukulu bya lwangu na vulehi bya minkarhi ya dyandza.
Tsala mitirho leyi kunguhatiweke kutani u ringanisa xilaveko ku suka eka tirhekhodo ta wena n'wini. Pimanisa sweswo na mati lama kumekaka hi tinguva hinkwato.
Kunguhatela leswi u nga ta swi endla loko mati lama hlayisiweke ma hunguteka. Vito ra phurovhinse ntsena a ri nge ku byeli sayizi ya thanki leyi u yi lavaka.
Hlayisa thanki yi funengetiwile, sefa tindhawu leti pfulekeke ku sivela switsotswana, naswona u hlayisa lwangu, tigatara na diverter. Hlayisa mati ya mpfula ma hambanile na tiphayiphi ta mati yo nwa.
Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The diversion needed depends on roof and system. Use supplier sizing/maintenance instructions; no one volume works for every roof.

A diverter does not make remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on demand, rain, roof area and duration of dry periods.

List intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare supply across the seasons.

Plan what to do when stored water gets low. A province name alone cannot tell you needed tank size.

Keep tank covered. Screen openings against insects; maintain roof, gutters, diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone does not guarantee drinking water. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
